title: SQL Fundamentals for Data Analysts
description: A hands-on introduction to exploring relational data in DB Browser for SQLite, built around a stable e-commerce Customers and Orders dataset.
target_audience: Beginner data analysts with no SQL experience

videos.title: Browse and Explore the Customers Table
videos.learning_objective: Open the Customers table, sort by customer_id, and filter by country to explore the data interactively.
videos.discovery_objective: Open the Customers table in the Browse Data tab, sort by the customer_id column header, and filter by the country column to show only matching rows.

exercise_artifact.description: Customers table with customer_id, customer_name, country, and signup_date.

videos.preview_text_hint: Next we will browse the Orders table and see how it relates to Customers.
key_concepts: A database table stores data in rows and columns.
The Browse Data tab shows table contents without writing SQL.
Column headers reveal the structure of a table.
Sorting and filtering are fast ways to explore a table interactively.

demo_plan.expected_observable_result: Browse Data tab becomes active and the data grid is visible.

demo_plan.action_description: Select the Customers table from the table dropdown
demo_plan.expected_observable_result: Customers table rows and columns appear in the grid.

demo_plan.action_description: Click the country filter box and type USA
demo_plan.expected_observable_result: Only rows where country equals USA remain visible.

script_beats.text: In this lesson, we open the Customers table, sort, and filter to explore the data interactively.
The Customers table shows 20 rows with columns customer_id, customer_name, country, signup_date. Sorting reorders the rows without changing the stored data.
We click the Browse Data tab.
The data grid is now visible. We can select a table here and view its rows without writing SQL.

action.detail: Browse Data tab becomes active and the data grid is visible.

script_beats.text: We see the Browse Data tab is active and the data grid is visible.

action.detail: Customers table in the table dropdown

script_beats.text: The Customers grid is loaded. Each row is a record, and the headers name the columns.

action.detail: Customers table rows and columns appear in the grid.

script_beats.text: We see the Customers grid is loaded and matches the schema.
We click the Customer_id column header.
The rows now reorder by Customer_id in ascending order. The stored data is unchanged; only the view is sorted.
We see the Customers table is sorted by Customer_id in ascending order.
We click the Country filter box and type USA.
The grid now shows only rows where Country matches USA. The status bar reflects the filtered count.

action.detail: Only rows where country equals USA remain visible.

script_beats.text: We see the Customers table filtered by Country. The status bar shows the matching count.
We opened, sorted, and filtered the Customers table. We can now explore any table interactively.

running_example.name: E-commerce Orders and Customers
running_example.description: A small online store dataset with a Customers table linked to an Orders table via customer_id.
